lesson.text: Quick memory: last unit, multiplying as scaling. Is 5 × 3/4 more or less than 5? Less: 3/4 is less than 1.
1/3 ÷ 2 shares one third into 2 equal parts. Each part is 1/6, because 6 of them make a whole.
4 ÷ 1/3 asks: how many thirds fit in 4? Each whole has 3 thirds, so 4 wholes have 4 × 3 = 12.
Stories: 3 kg of seeds fill 12 bags of 1/4 kg, because 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12. And 1/2 L of juice shared by 4 friends is 1/2 ÷ 4 = 1/8 L each.
Try it in the world: you have 3 stacks of blocks and each tower needs 1/4 of a stack. How many towers? 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12. Next: percentages.

exercises.hint: Share a half into 2 equal parts.
exercises.explain: Half of a half is a quarter: 1/2 ÷ 2 = 1/4.
Each whole has 2 halves, so 3 wholes have 6.

exercises.hint: How many quarters are in 2 wholes?
exercises.explain: Each whole has 4 quarters, so 2 wholes have 8. Check: 8 × 1/4 = 2.

exercises.hint: Share one third into 4 equal parts. How many of those make a whole?
exercises.explain: Each third splits into 4, so a whole has 12 parts: 1/12. Check: 1/12 × 4 = 1/3.

exercises.hint: Dividing by a half is not the same as halving.
exercises.explain: 6 ÷ 1/2 asks how many halves fit in 6: 12. Halving 6 is 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

exercises.prompt: Nell has 5 kg of flour. How many bags of 1/3 kg can she fill?
exercises.hint: How many thirds in 1 kg? In 5 kg?

exercises.prompt: 1/4 L of juice is shared equally among 3 friends. How much does each friend get, in litres?

exercises.hint: One shares a half into 5 parts; the other counts the halves in 5.
